subject.title: [Feature Request]: Multi-lane concurrency support for sub-agents via sessions_spawn

question: Should sub-agent isolation use caller-selected lanes, agent-owned concurrency limits, or a unified bounded scheduler abstraction?
rationale: The internal queue supports named lanes, but exposing them to models and configuration affects fairness, resource safety, observability, and several overlapping scheduling proposals.

options.title: Unified bounded scheduler
options.body: Define validated isolation groups with per-group and aggregate limits plus shared observability, avoiding parallel scheduling contracts.

options.title: Narrow spawn lanes
options.body: Expose a validated `sessions_spawn.lane` and per-lane caps while retaining the existing global aggregate cap.

options.title: Retain shared pool
options.body: Keep one public sub-agent pool and improve internal fairness without exposing caller-selected routing.

recommendation.title: Unified bounded scheduler
recommendation.body: Define validated isolation groups with per-group and aggregate limits plus shared observability, avoiding parallel scheduling contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature introduction, concurrency refactor, ACP isolation work, and live issue discussion make this the strongest available decision owner.
